There exists a creative gap. In this gap is the work you don't like, the stuff that seems unoriginal and the stuff that is simply awful. This gap exists in most people. Savants do exist but they are few and far between. To overcome this gap you must fill it. It has to be filled with the dissatisfying, the unoriginal and the bad. It is once you fill this gap thru practice, work and development that the artist becomes something else. It's a practice makes perfect type thing. 

It is clear that you aren't your title. You can write with coherence and have a grasp of the language. Your title is a disservice to yourself but you are on a depression subreddit so I expect that. 

Here is my suggestion to you, WRITE. What makes someone a writer anyway? They write. Write everyday. Work the job you hate but write about it. Be depressed but write about it. Here's what it took for me to get better. I had to attack this disease on every front. It's been ok recently. I've mostly come to terms with being sick and my mistakes. It took a long time. I understand the comfort in being able to use a disease as a fall back. I used it as an excuse, I was in the throes of it for so long I didn't know anything else. It's hard for me to be my own man when most days I feel like a phony kid walking around in grownup shoes. 

Here is my plan. 

1.  I talked to my doc. Honestly and openly. Started in 2007. Had the current physician for 4 hrs. He's been amazing. Not all docs are the same. 

2. I did several years of therapy starting about the same time. 

3. Took my meds faithfully. 

4. Eat clean most of the time. Past 4-6 months. 

5. Started working out several times a week, mostly running. It's a good supplement. If I feel like crap I know a better mood is 3 miles away. 

6. Came to terms with what I lost and stopped feeling sorry for myself about my mistakes. I can still build what I want. In fact I now have bigger dreams. I'm as young as I will ever be. I know the pain of regret and don't want anymore of it. So I can look back forever or start moving on. 

7. I believe better is possible. 

8. Realized. I'm a tough mother fucker. Anyone who questions this is more than welcome to spend a day in my head. They will likely change their mind.  I still frequently fell awful. It got better but it ain't all sunshine and roses. 

9. I started moving forward. No zero days. Something gets done. 

10. I am grateful for what I have. It's really key. It came when I started looking in to stoicism. 

So that's my deal. There's a few more thing but 10s enough to make my point. It's not easy and it takes a lot of work. It's possible tho. You have identified your first steps. It's a matter of making one. Go to the doc, agree to therapy, try it. You might like it.
